newsitem.title: USA: U.S. says no decision on Clinton-Yeltsin summit.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says no decision on Clinton-Yeltsin summit.

text.p: There has been no decision on the timing or venue of any 1998 summit meeting between U.S. President Bill Clinton and Russian President Boris Yeltsin, a White House spokesman said on Monday.
He was commenting on a report by Russia's Itar-Tass news agency that Yeltsin would host Clinton in Moscow at a summit next March or April that would focus on energy.

Itar-Tass, quoting Russian Russian First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov, said the Clinton-Yeltsin summit would precede a Moscow meeting, also on energy issues, of the Group of Seven leading industrial nations and Russia.

The White House spokesman said the G7 and Russia agreed at last month's Summit of the Eight in Denver to hold a meeting on energy issues next year but this was not now expected to take place at the head of state level.
"Separately, the president and President Yeltsin had a casual discussion (in Denver) about a summit in 1998, but nothing has been fixed," he said.

Clinton and Yeltsin met last month on the sidelines of the Denver summit, which brought together the leaders of the G7 -- Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and the United States -- as well as Yeltsin.
Their last formal summit meeting took place in March in Helsinki, Finland.
